name: US federal employment law thresholds by employee count
description: Employee-count thresholds that trigger US federal employment laws. Each record is one law at one threshold, stating the trigger point, what the law requires, and how employees are counted for that statute.
licence: Facts extracted from vendor blog posts; thresholds are statutory and not copyrightable

records.requirement: protects those with disabilities from being discriminated against for employment-related opportunities
records.counting_note: part-time and temporary employees are included in the head-count calculation
records.source_quote: Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) The <https://www.ada.gov/topics/intro-to-ada/#employment> Americans with Disabilities Act protects those with disabilities from being discriminated against for employment-related opportunities, from recruiting, hiring, job training, promotions, and pay, to social activities that are provided to staff members.

records.requirement: you cannot discriminate against (or harass) employees or applicants age 40 or older simply due to their age
records.counting_note: part-time and temporary employees are included in the head-count calculation
records.source_quote: Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA) Per the <https://www.eeoc.gov/eeoc/publications/age.cfm> Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA), you cannot discriminate against (or harass) employees or applicants age 40 or older simply due to their age.

records.requirement: Organizations with 50 or more employees and $50,000 in government contracts must have an AAP
records.source_quote: Affirmative Action Affirmative action plans (AAPs) define a company’s policies and procedures on training programs, outreach efforts, and business practices that promote qualified minorities, women, people with disabilities, and veterans for equal employment opportunities. Organizations with 50 or more employees and $50,000 in government contracts must have an AAP.

records.requirement: Age discrimination protection for workers 40 and older
records.source_quote: Age Discrimination in Employment Act

records.requirement: you cannot discriminate
records.counting_note: Unless otherwise specified, part-time and temporary employees are included in the head-count calculation
records.source_quote: Here are the laws that apply to employers with 20+ employees in any industry affecting commerce. Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA) Per the <https://www.eeoc.gov/eeoc/publications/age.cfm> Age Discrimination in Employment Act (ADEA), you cannot discriminate against (or harass) employees or applicants age 40 or older simply due to their age.

records.requirement: your company becomes what’s called an 'applicable large employer' (ALE). In addition to offering health insurance, you’ll need to demonstrate your HR compliance to the IRS every year by filing Forms 1095-C and 1094-C.
records.counting_note: Seasonal staff working less than 120 days a year do not count toward your headcount for ACA compliance purposes.
records.source_quote: Once you hit the 50 employee threshold, your company becomes what’s called an “applicable large employer” (ALE).

records.requirement: you to provide rest breaks and accommodations (in a location other than a bathroom) for nursing mothers to express breast milk for up to 1 year after the child’s birth
records.counting_note: Employers with fewer than 50 employees may be exempt if they can demonstrate an undue hardship
records.source_quote: Break Time for Nursing Mothers <https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/73-flsa-break-time-nursing-mothers> Break Time for Nursing Mothers is a sub-section to the ACA that requires you to provide rest breaks and accommodations (in a location other than a bathroom) for nursing mothers to express breast milk for up to 1 year after the child’s birth.

records.requirement: you cannot discharge an employee simply because their wages have been garnished for a debt
records.source_quote: Consumer Credit Protection Act (CCPA) The <https://webapps.dol.gov/elaws/elg/garnish.htm#BasicPro> Consumer Credit Protection Act (CCPA) says you cannot discharge an employee simply because their wages have been garnished for a debt.

records.requirement: requires employers to offer continuation coverage of employer-sponsored group health insurance to eligible employees and their dependents when coverage would otherwise be lost due to certain events such as termination
records.counting_note: part-time and temporary employees are included in the head-count calculation
records.source_quote: Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (COBRA)

records.requirement: Develop formal procedures for workforce changes and annual EEO reporting
records.source_quote: EEO-1

records.requirement: requires you to annually submit employment data categorized by race/ethnicity, gender, and job category to the EEOC
records.counting_note: part-time and temporary employees are included in the head-count calculation
records.source_quote: EEO-1 Report The <https://www.eeoc.gov/data/eeo-data-collections> EEO-1 Report requires you to annually submit employment data categorized by race/ethnicity, gender, and job category to the EEOC.

records.requirement: businesses over a certain size submit a headcount report including race, gender, and role information on an annual basis.
records.counting_note: the law does not distinguish between full-time or part-time workers.
records.source_quote: The EEOC organization requires that businesses over a certain size submit a headcount report including race, gender, and role information on an annual basis. While private businesses don’t have to worry about demographic reporting until reaching 100 employees, federal contractors need to comply once they hit the 50 employee threshold.

records.requirement: you must provide equal compensation to anyone who performs equal work within the same workplace, regardless of gender
records.source_quote: Equal Pay Act (EPA) According to the <https://www.eeoc.gov/eeoc/publications/fs-epa.cfm> Equal Pay Act (EPA), you must provide equal compensation to anyone who performs equal work within the same workplace, regardless of gender.

records.requirement: if you are a private employer, you cannot use a lie detector test for pre-employment screening or during the course of employment unless you meet certain exceptions
records.source_quote: Employee Polygraph Protection Act (EPPA)

records.requirement: your benefit plans must meet minimum standards outlined in the act, which include regulations for participation, vesting, benefit accrual and funding, fiduciary responsibilities, grievance process
records.source_quote: Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) Under the <https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/retirement/erisa> Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA), your benefit plans must meet minimum standards outlined in the act, which include regulations for participation, vesting, benefit accrual and funding, fiduciary responsibilities, grievance process, and so on.

records.requirement: you must take certain steps prior to using consumer reports (including standard background checks) to make employment decisions
records.source_quote: Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) Per the <https://www.ftc.gov/tips-advice/business-center/guidance/using-consumer-reports-what-employers-need-know> Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), you must take certain steps prior to using consumer reports (including standard background checks) to make employment decisions.

records.requirement: requires nonexempt employees to be paid at least a minimum wage and overtime wages
records.source_quote: Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) Among other things, the <https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/flsa> Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) requires nonexempt employees to be paid at least a minimum wage and overtime wages.

records.requirement: requires you to provide eligible employees with unpaid, job-protected leave for specified family and medical reasons
records.counting_note: part-time and temporary employees are included in the head-count calculation
records.source_quote: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) The <https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla/employer-guide> Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) requires you to provide eligible employees with unpaid, job-protected leave for specified family and medical reasons.

versions.source_quote: Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) The <https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla/employer-guide> Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) requires you to provide eligible employees with unpaid, job-protected leave for specified family and medical reasons.
The Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) requires companies with 50 or more employees to offer its staff up to 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave.

records.requirement: requires you to only hire and retain employees who are legally authorized to work in the United States
records.source_quote: Immigration Reform and Control Act (IRCA) The <https://www.congress.gov/bill/99th-congress/senate-bill/1200> Immigration Reform and Control Act (IRCA) requires you to only hire and retain employees who are legally authorized to work in the United States.

records.requirement: you cannot discharge, intimidate, or threaten to discharge an employee summoned to serve as a juror in federal court
records.source_quote: Jury System Improvements Act According to the <https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/1875> Jury System Improvements Act , you cannot discharge, intimidate, or threaten to discharge an employee summoned to serve as a juror in federal court.

records.requirement: requires you to provide a safe workplace, maintain records of work-related injuries, post required information, and train employees regarding safety hazards
records.source_quote: Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSH Act) The <https://www.osha.gov/Publications/3439at-a-glance.pdf> Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSH Act) requires you to provide a safe workplace, maintain records of work-related injuries, post required information, and train employees regarding safety hazards.

records.full_name: Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act
records.requirement: when an employee returns from military service or training, you are required to provide them with either their former job or a comparable job
records.source_quote: Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) The <https://www.dol.gov/agencies/vets/programs/userra/USERRA%20Pocket%20Guide> Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA) says that when an employee returns from military service or training, you are required to provide them with either their former job or a comparable job to what they had prior to military duty.

records.full_name: Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act
records.requirement: you are required to provide a 60-day advance written notice to affected employees
records.counting_note: part-time and temporary employees are included in the head-count calculation
records.source_quote: Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act Per the <https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/termination/plantclosings> Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification (WARN) Act , if your plant closes or you have a mass layoff, you are required to provide a 60-day advance written notice to affected employees.
